chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reproached a people for publicizing (al-itha'ah) in His saying, Mighty and Majestic:
And when there comes to them news of security or fear, they publicize it.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'al-itha'ah' refer to in the context of spreading news?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the prohibition of indiscriminate news dissemination to the Quranic verse in Surah An-Nisa (4:83), where Allah reproached those who publicized matters of security or fear. In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith is often contextualized within the era of political instability (such as the Great Deviation or Ghaybah) to advise believers on maintaining discretion and preventing the spread of rumors that could incite panic or reveal strategic secrets.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Blamed a people for the publicising in the Words of the Mighty and Majestic
[4:83] And when there comes to them news of security or fear they publicise it.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has criticized people for publicizing confidential matters in His words, “
When they receive any news of peace or war, they announce it in public. . . [4:83]
Therefore, be on your guard against publicity of confidential matters.’”
